title: Symbol Identity Integration Audit
description: Source-level audit of whether the visual catalog, identity crosswalk, notation mappings, and association bridge can share a stable occurrence identity without a new parallel symbol system.

identity_contract.requirement: A stable occurrence identity must survive across all four systems without a new parallel symbol system.
identity_contract.governing_rule: Never convert an absent mapping into an inferred identity merely because the glyph looks similar. Record missing mappings as explicit nulls, not inferred values.

architectural_corrections.correction: Do not make Metamath name the universal identity. Separate identifier responsibilities:

identifier_separation.occurrence_id: Specific observed glyph in a source document

rationale: One mathematical symbol can have multiple visual representations
One Unicode character can have multiple font/style variants
Some ZIP assets may have no Metamath chart counterpart
A glyph's mathematical role depends on its expression context

implementation_sequence.acceptance: Every mapping has provenance and status
Stable occurrence identity and source provenance
Identity fields consumed without automatic verification
Existing behavior preserved; no premature state promotion

certification_gates.independence_rule: Passing G2 must not imply G3, and passing G3 must not imply G4 or G5

recommendation: Before modifying AssociationRecord, build the expanded crosswalk and establish its identity contract. Otherwise, you risk adding fields to the bridge that encode assumptions the reference catalog cannot yet support. The goal should be to reuse the existing 3,301-image catalog, four-entry crosswalk, 82 Wolfram mappings, 77 SymPy mappings, and existing AST infrastructure - not create competing implementations. The next meaningful milestone is a provenance-backed glyph identity registry, with zero inferred mappings and explicit unresolved identities.
